widget.MipCharge.title: Charge from a minimum-ionising particle
widget.MipCharge.xsec: Sensor cross-section with a particle crossing it; dots stand for the electron-hole pairs created along the track
widget.MipCharge.xsecLabel: {t} µm of silicon (dots: schematic, not one per pair)
widget.MipCharge.view: Distribution of the collected charge for a minimum-ionising particle, with the noise threshold marked
widget.MipCharge.schematic: Schematic Landau-shaped distribution (Moyal form): asymmetric, with a long tail towards large charge.
widget.MipCharge.note: Mean energy loss 0.39 keV/µm, one pair per 3.6 eV: 108 pairs/µm on average. The most probable value is lower, about 80 pairs/µm for thick sensors, because of the long tail (smaller still for very thin sensors). S/N = most probable charge / ENC. The distribution shape is schematic.
widget.BiasDepletion.title: Bias voltage and depletion
widget.BiasDepletion.full: Fully depleted: the whole thickness collects charge. More voltage only makes the field stronger and the drift faster.
widget.BiasDepletion.partial: Partially depleted: charge made in the undepleted part is not collected.
widget.BiasDepletion.xsec: Sensor cross-section with the depleted region shaded and the electric field profile on the right
widget.BiasDepletion.xsecCap: Cross-section: junction on top, backside below. Shaded and labelled = depleted; hatched = undepleted. Right: field E(x).
widget.BiasDepletion.plot: Depleted width as a function of bias voltage
widget.BiasDepletion.note: N_eff = 1/(q µ_n ρ), W = √(2 ε₀ε_r (V_bi + V) / (q N_eff)) capped at d, V_fd = q N_eff d² / (2 ε₀ε_r) − V_bi, with ε_r = 11.9, V_bi = 0.6 V, µ_n = 1350 cm²/Vs. Charge = 80 µm⁻¹ × W; leakage ∝ W (schematic).
widget.ChargeSharing.title: Charge sharing between pixels
widget.ChargeSharing.view: Five pixels in a row with the share of the diffusion cloud collected by each; the true hit position and the position estimate are marked
widget.ChargeSharing.cap: Percentages: share of the charge in each pixel. Dashed bell: the cloud. Solid line: true position. Thick line: estimate.
widget.ChargeSharing.note: Share in pixel k = ½[erf((x_{k+1} − x₀)/σ√2) − erf((x_k − x₀)/σ√2)]. Binary readout gives p/√12; the centroid does much better when the cloud spans two pixels (σ not much smaller than p), but is biased and noisy when it does not. 2 % noise per pixel; simulated.
widget.TestbeamResiduals.title: Test-beam residuals
widget.TestbeamResiduals.view: Side view of the beam telescope with the device under test in the middle and one simulated event: measured hits, the fitted track and the DUT hit
widget.TestbeamResiduals.viewCap: Last simulated event (transverse offsets exaggerated). Open dots: telescope hits; line: fitted track; ring on the DUT: measured hit (the open dot on the line is the prediction).
widget.TestbeamResiduals.hist: Histogram of residuals with a Gaussian curve
widget.TestbeamResiduals.histCap: Bars: simulated residuals. Curve: Gaussian with the fitted width.
widget.TestbeamResiduals.note: σ_res = √(σ_DUT² + σ_pred²). σ_pred comes from a telescope-only simulation: about σ_tel/√N for a centred DUT, plus multiple scattering θ₀ = 13.6 MeV/p · √(x/X₀)(1 + 0.038 ln(x/X₀)) per 50 µm silicon plane. Efficiency fixed at 99 %. Simulated example only.
widget.TrackCurvature.title: Curvature of a track in a magnetic field
widget.TrackCurvature.view: Top view of a tracker with a track bending {sense} in a magnetic field pointing out of the page
widget.TrackCurvature.convention: Positive charge turns clockwise when B points out of the page.
widget.TrackCurvature.cap: Tracker of radius 1.2 m. Dashed: the full circle of radius r. The segment s is the sagitta of the chord L.
widget.TrackCurvature.noField: No field, no bend: momentum cannot be measured from the curvature.
widget.TrackCurvature.looper: Low momentum: the track curls up inside the tracker.
widget.TrackCurvature.straight: Nearly straight (sagitta below 1 mm): hard to measure.
widget.TrackCurvature.ok: A clear bend: the momentum can be measured from the curvature.
widget.TrackCurvature.note: r [m] = p [GeV/c] / (0.3 B [T]); s = L²/(8r); σ_p/p = p σ_x √(720/(N+4)) / (0.3 B L²) with σ_x = 10 µm, N = 10 points: grows in proportion to p and falls as 1/B (schematic).
widget.ParticleSignatures.title: Particle signatures in the detector layers
widget.ParticleSignatures.view: End view of the detector layers, from the inside out: tracker, electromagnetic calorimeter, hadron calorimeter, muon system. Layers with a signal:
widget.ParticleSignatures.cap: Qualitative. Line: track. Filled wedge: energy deposit (darker = larger share). Squares: muon hits. Dashed arrow: missing momentum.
widget.ParticleSignatures.question: Which particle left this signature?
widget.ParticleSignatures.hidden: Layers that show a signal (particle hidden)
widget.ParticleSignatures.why.e: A track in the tracker, then the whole energy stops in the electromagnetic calorimeter. The track tells it from a photon.
widget.ParticleSignatures.why.g: The shower is fully in the electromagnetic calorimeter, but there is no track: a photon, not an electron.
widget.ParticleSignatures.why.mu: A track, only small deposits in the calorimeters, and hits in the outermost muon system. Only the muon gets that far.
widget.ParticleSignatures.why.pi: A track, a small deposit in the electromagnetic calorimeter and most of the energy in the hadron calorimeter.
widget.ParticleSignatures.why.n: The shower sits in the hadron calorimeter and there is no track: neutral, strongly interacting.
widget.ParticleSignatures.why.nu: Nothing in any layer. Only the missing momentum betrays it. A neutral hadron, by contrast, would show a hadronic shower.
widget.ParticleSignatures.note: Qualitative: ECAL share ≈ 1 for e and γ, ≈ 0.3 for hadrons, minimum-ionising deposits for the muon (≈ 0.3 GeV ECAL, ≈ 2 GeV HCAL). Fluctuations scale as 1/√E.
